title: Who can apply (ukri.org)
text:
This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
Who is eligible to apply
Project lead
The project lead for this funding opportunity must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) funding for the duration of the grant. Before applying for funding, please check the UKRI eligibility criteria .
Project leads from the following organisations are not eligible for this funding opportunity:
UK-based business, third sector or government bodies
non-UK organisations
The project lead must ensure that they contribute an appropriate proportion of their time to the overall leadership and coordination of the grant, in addition to any time allocated to research and knowledge mobilisation activities.
Applications may be submitted jointly by more than one applicant. In such cases, one person must be regarded as the project lead taking the lead responsibility for the conduct of the project and the observance of the terms and conditions.
Correspondence regarding the application and award will be addressed to the project lead only (and in the case of any grant agreement, to their research organisation).
Project co-leads
Your application must include at least one project co-lead from business, the third sector or government bodies based in the UK, subject to ESRC eligibility and costing rules .
As an exception for this centre, you may allocate more than the usual 30% of total costs (at 100% FEC) to non-academic partners where clearly justified, and while remaining within the total budget available for this funding opportunity.
The combined time commitment of research staff from non-academic partners can also exceed one year full time equivalent (FTE) for the duration of the project. This flexibility will enable the meaningful involvement of key local, regional and national stakeholders, whose participation is critical to the centre’s effective operation and capacity to deliver outcomes.
If you wish to exceed the 30% cost threshold or the combined time commitment cap, you must clearly justify this in your application, specifically within the ‘Justification of resources’ section. We also strongly encourage you to explain your planned approach and its rationale when answering the application questions on ‘Applicant and team capability to deliver’ and ‘Working collaboratively with partners and stakeholders’.
Eligible costs remain the same as those outlined in the ESRC project co-leads from UK business, third sector or government organisations policy . As with all ESRC awards, the lead research organisation will retain responsibility for the management and oversight of all funds.
Applications can also include project co-leads based in non-UK research organisations. See details of eligible organisations and costs .
Applications which include project co-leads from the UK business sector or from third sector organisations must ensure compliance with the UK subsidy control framework. More information can be found in the ESRC Project Co-Leads from UK Business, Third Sector or Government Organisations Policy .
All project co-leads must make a significant contribution to the centre.
Who is not eligible to apply
You may be involved in only one application as a project lead and a maximum of two applications as project co-leads.
Defra (as funder) and devolved governments (Welsh Government, Scottish Government and Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs in Northern Ireland) (as partners), whether as a whole, or through specific individuals or teams (including at regional and local level), cannot be named as a project co-lead or as a project partner on any application. As a funder or partner of the funding opportunity, this would constitute a conflict of interest. Funders and partners will instead engage with the successful centre through formal governance arrangements, and with the successful grant. If you have specific questions you would like to explore for your application then get in touch with ESRC.
Resubmissions
We will not accept uninvited resubmissions of projects that have been submitted to UK Research and Innovation (UKRI). Find out more about UKRI’s resubmission policy .
Equality, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants. We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
career breaks
support for people with caring responsibilities
flexible working
alternative working patterns
UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support for UKRI applicants and grant holders during the application and assessment process.
Remit
We wish to ensure that the centre can effectively drive forward policy evaluation, economic analysis and insight into policy communication and acceptability. You must demonstrate that the Centre’s vision, leadership and programme of work has the appropriate balance of research, social science expertise and skills to deliver these outcomes.
Please refer to the list of research areas that fall within ESRC’s remit for further information.
Complete and submit the remit query form , if you are unsure whether the majority of your proposed research falls within the remit of ESRC.
